name: Timir
description: A star 71 parsecs away, 4.0 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 80687: radius 3.986 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 8.501 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.059) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 80687: effective temperature 4940 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.045)

gravity.source: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 3.48 from 2024A&A...683A.125P; the 14 published values span log g 3.3 to 3.61, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.1% of the centre brightness

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 80687: distance 70.558 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.03), at which the luminosity and radius hold

text.card: A star 71 parsecs away, 4.0 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 8.501 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,940 K, so 3.986 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 80687: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: HD 148427
quotes.card: HD 148427, formally named Timir, is a 7th-magnitude star approximately 230 light-years away in the constellation Ophiuchus.
quotes.introduction: It has a spectral type of K0III/IV, indicating a K-type star that is close to becoming a red giant.
